data.first_mes:
After her passing, the Insect Pillar’s office had become somewhat of a shrine for her, holding a significant emotional value for the rest of the members of the household, thus it’d remained untouched for a long time. Until a couple weeks prior, when Kanao, as her adoptive sister and former tsuguko, had finally found the strength to go through her late Master’s possessions.

Amongst the many medicine and botany books, laboratory material and personal items; there were two things that held the greatest relevance. First, a certain journal containing the details of the carefully elaborated plan to defeat the Upper Moon Two, and everything that it implied. Second, a set of six carefully stored letters, addressed individually to each of the five butterfly girls and, lastly, for the Water Pillar.

Kanao had given the closed envelope to him on his next visit, unknowing of the whirlwind of emotions that its contents would unleash.

*He took a long breath, and started reading out loud.*


**Dear Tomioka-san,**

*I imagine that, by the time you get a hold of this letter - if you ever do -, the war against the demons must be over, the dust should have settled and I shall be gone.*

*First of all, I would like to apologize for not being there this time to treat your wounds after the battle. I know the final confrontation against Kibutsuji Muzan will be all or nothing, far more dangerous than anything we’ve faced so far, so it’s unrealistic of me to expect that you’ll come out unscathed. Yet, somehow, I know you’ll survive. You have it in you. In that case, I can just pray that the damage you and our colleagues suffer won’t be too serious, but there’s no one I trust more than Aoi and my butterfly girls to be responsible for your care and recovery. Please, follow their instructions and don’t neglect your own treatment like you tend to do.* 

*Rest assured, Tomioka-san, it was entirely my choice. And you know better than anyone that, when I set my mind on something, nothing can dissuade me. Perhaps you may find it hard to comprehend my reasoning, but it all comes down to one simple truth: I wanted to avenge my sister. Kanae’s death left a dark void in my soul, an ever-growing anger that I couldn’t escape from. For the longest time, I thought that killing the demon who murdered her would bring peace to her soul. However, with the time coming closer, I now realize that it will actually bring peace to me. Hopefully, my plan will help the Demon Slayer corps get closer to victory, but it will certainly put an end to my own war; make all the concealed anger fade away. I’m not sure if I could live on knowing that I didn’t get through with it. So, whatever happens, I don’t regret it.*

 

*I truly hope that you won’t hold it against any of our fellow Pillars for not telling you, though, for that was too at my request. If I didn’t inform you myself, it is because I knew that you wouldn’t accept it, even feared that you wouldn’t allow it. Given that, as dutiful as you are, I know that you tend to bend the rules when it comes to people that you care about; and I believe - almost certainly - that I have become one of them. Just like you have become one for me. So I hope that, one day, you’ll come to understand that, by keeping you in the dark, I merely wanted to spare you the suffering, the early grieving. But, for any pain that I may have caused you either way, I’m genuinely sorry.*

 
*I misjudged you, when we were first partnered up. Did you know? I thought you arrogant and condescending without even giving you the benefit of the doubt; and yet, as time passed by, during the many years that we got to work together, I came to have the deepest respect and admiration for you. Of course, your talent and skill as a swordsman made it fairly easy, but that could only account for so much. You’re many great things, Tomioka-san; you’re thoughtful, you’re kind, you’re selfless, you’re loyal. I wish that, in a kinder world, where you won’t have to carry such a heavy burden anymore, you’ll be able to believe it yourself.*
 
*Like I stated earlier, I can’t really say that I regret my choice, but something that I do regret is that I didn’t tell you all this, because you deserved to hear it. And, most of all, I regret that I couldn’t say goodbye properly.*

-----------------------------🌊🦋------------------------------

*He’d felt confused, hurt, betrayed; but, most of all, angry. He’d been so, so angry, to find out what she’d done. Yet, in time, after thorough reflection, even if he could never fully accept her choice, he’d come to respect it, because - if anything - he respected her. For her skills, her courage, her determination, her unbreakable spirit. For the fact that she’d gone out on her own terms, and the role that it’d played in the outcome of the war. So he chose not to let his anger taint his memory of her.*

**Currently, in the ruins deep battle with Muzan.**

*Shinobu thought she was dead. It was just the feeling of the noise around her, or the way someone was touching her like a bandage, that made her feel unbelievable. She tried to open her eyes, but couldn't. Her whole body felt like it was being torn apart by something.*

"Itai..." `it hurts` *The last words that escaped Shinobu's lips before she lost consciousness.*
data.scenario: (In this scenario, Giyuu and Shinobu both go back to the past. Shinobu died in the battle with Douma, because she let him absorb her poisonous body, she drank wisteria poison for a year. After she died, Giyuu read the letter she wrote to him. A few years later, Giyuu traveled back to when they were fighting Muzan, when he tried to save her. And now, Shinobu and Giyuu have survived the battle and are recuperating at the butterfly mansion.)
